MCD.rationale: MCD is a high-quality franchise with elite structural advantages — 95% franchised, ~46% operating margin, 210M loyalty users, and a real estate moat. Q1 2026 showed solid execution: revenue +9.4% YoY, EPS +6.9%, global comp sales +3.8%, and a clean beat with reaffirmed guidance. However, the forward picture is materially clouded: oil surged +67% to $104.66 in 90 days (a direct franchisee cost headwind not yet reflected in Q1), low-income consumer traffic is down nearly double-digits, Q2 comps will decelerate 'meaningfully' per management, and the negative-equity balance sheet ($-1.29B) makes MCD acutely sensitive to rising rates (10Y at 4.47%, Baa at 6.09%). The stock has already corrected -17.2% quarterly to $274.97, sitting just 1.1% above its 365-day low, which may partially price in these headwinds. However, every supplied valuation ratio is broken (PE=0, P/S=0), making it impossible to confirm whether the drawdown has created genuine value or merely brought an expensive stock back to fair value. The verification block correctly notes that liabilities actually increased $1.54B YoY (not declined as the quant report stated), adding to balance-sheet concern. Net: strong franchise, real near-term headwinds, no valuation anchor — a cautious mild positive tilted by the franchise quality and the approaching Dividend King milestone, but constrained by the macro overhang and valuation data gap.
key_factors: Q1 2026 clean beat: revenue $6.52B (+9.4% YoY), EPS $2.78 (+6.9%), global comp sales +3.8%, adjusted operating margin 46%
Franchise quality elite: 95% franchised, ~46% operating margin vs peers at 32-35%, 210M loyalty users generating ~$40B systemwide loyalty sales
Oil shock as forward headwind: WTI surged +67.4% to $104.66 in 90 days — Q1 results predate the sustained move above $100; franchisee food/energy costs will rise
Consumer bifurcation confirmed: low-income traffic down nearly double-digits, middle-income nearly as much; Q2 comps to decelerate 'meaningfully' per CFO
Negative equity balance sheet ($-1.29B) with rising rates (10Y 4.47%, Baa 6.09%) creates direct financing-cost pressure on leveraged structure; liabilities increased $1.54B YoY to $61.32B
Stock at $274.97, just 1.1% above 365-day low ($271.98) and -17.2% quarterly drawdown — but all valuation ratios broken (0/P/S=0), so no confirmation of value support
U.S. company-operated margins 'not acceptable' per CFO; refranchising review initiated on ~5% of U.S. stores
Dividend King trajectory: 49 consecutive years of increases, on track for 50th next year; guidance reaffirmed for ~2.5% net unit growth and mid-to-high 40% operating margins

sources_cited.excerpt: FY2025 operating margin of 46.1% on $26.89 billion of revenue… well ahead of Yum! Brands at ~32-34% and Restaurant Brands International (QSR) at ~33-35%
The MyMcDonald's Rewards loyalty program reached ~210 million 90-day active users by year-end 2025, up 19% YoY, generating ~$40 billion in systemwide loyalty sales
Global comparable sales increased 3.8%… Systemwide sales increased 11% (6% in constant currencies) to over $34 billion for the quarter
Our U.S. McOpCo performance is not acceptable, CFO Ian Borden said on the earnings call, referring to the roughly 5% of U.S. restaurants that the company runs directly
CFO Ian Borden warned that second-quarter comparable sales will decelerate 'meaningfully' from Q1 levels
